question: An engineer asks the agent to add comprehensive tests to a legacy codebase. The agent maps the structure with Glob and Grep, identifies the billing module as the highest-impact area, and builds a prioritized plan that starts there. While writing billing tests, the agent uses Read on the billing code and discovers that every total depends on an untested date-handling module that the plan did not list. How should the agent's plan respond to this discovery?

options.text: Add a subtask to test the date-handling module and move it ahead of the remaining billing tests, since the billing results depend on that module.
options.reason: The guide says that an adaptive plan generates subtasks from what each step discovers, and that the prioritized plan adapts as dependencies are discovered.

options.text: Keep the original order of the plan and put the date-handling module on a follow-up list for after all planned modules are tested.
options.reason: This treats the plan as fixed and ignores the discovered dependency until the end, so the plan does not adapt as dependencies are discovered, as the guide requires.

options.text: Replace the prioritized plan with an alphabetical pass over all modules, so that the agent reaches the date-handling module without special handling.
options.reason: The guide says to identify high-impact areas and follow a prioritized plan; an alphabetical pass drops the priorities and ignores what the discovery revealed.

options.text: Stop the current plan, map the entire codebase again from the start, and build a completely new plan before writing any more tests.
options.reason: The guide describes a prioritized plan that adapts as dependencies are discovered; it does not call for discarding the existing map and plan after each new finding.
